subject: Action: Evidence checklist for 'Do Not Use for Model Improvement' (DNM) — next steps
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@therabio.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: TheraBio Legal <legal@therabio.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Do Not Use for Model Improvement — evidence and routing questions

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we liked the latency profile and the routing controls. As part of the procurement loop, our legal/privacy team needs to confirm a couple of things before we can sign the DPA redlines (attached). High-level asks: 

- We need a clear "Do Not Use for Model Improvement" (DNM) commitment that covers both prompt and response content (no training, no model tuning, no derivatives used for any model improvement).
- We need evidence you can produce to substantiate that commitment: audit logs, KV/prefix cache behavior, and a sample attestation.
- Subprocessor inventory and whether any subprocessors have access to decrypted prompt/response content.
- Options for EU residency or express routing so data never leaves the EU; if transfers are required, confirm standard contractual clauses (SCCs) / transfer mechanisms and whether you will sign them.

Can you confirm what you can provide and an estimated delivery timeline? I've attached our redlines for context.

Best,
Emma
--
Emma Li
Head of IT Security, TheraBio
emma@therabio.com
Attachment: TheraBio_DPA_redlines.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@therabio.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Do Not Use for Model Improvement — evidence and routing questions

Emma — thanks for the clear list and for sharing the redlines. Looping Monica (privacy/legal) and Laura (security/evidence) so we can respond comprehensively. Quick summary of what we can commit and next actions: 

- DNM commitment: Redwood can sign a clause that we will not use customer prompts/responses for model improvement. We already support a customer opt-out workflow and a contractual attestation variant; Monica will propose language.

- Evidence: we can produce an evidence pack that includes: one-page attestation, export of relevant audit logs (access + export events), and a subprocessor access log for the relevant time window. Laura will own the evidence pack runbook.

- Subprocessors: we maintain an up-to-date inventory (AWS EU regions, GCP EU partner, and two telemetry vendors). We'll provide the CSV export and indicate which subprocessors process decrypted customer content.

- Residency / transfers: we support EU-region routing for inference for most models; where a model variant isn't available in-region we provide fallback routing controls and explicit notification. For transfers, we use SCCs and will sign where required — Monica can confirm signatures and any required amendments.

Next steps / timeline: 
1) Monica to propose DNM clause and a short attestation template (by Wed EOD).
2) Laura to prepare the evidence pack and subprocessor CSV (ETA Thu).
3) I'll collate and send a single package for your review (ETA Fri morning).

If you need anything faster (e.g., an initial attestation today) let me know and I can escalate.

Cheers,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@therabio.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed DNM clause + SCC confirmation

Emma — following up with the legal view and a proposed clause below. I kept it short so your procurement team can fold it into the DPA redlines: 

"Do Not Use for Model Improvement (DNM): Provider shall not use, analyze, aggregate, or otherwise process Customer Content (including prompts and generated responses) for the purpose of training, improving, or tuning Provider models, nor shall Provider allow any Subprocessor to do so without prior written consent from Customer."

A few clarifications: 
- This covers both prompts and generated outputs.
- We will provide a signed attestation on company letterhead upon execution.
- Subprocessor access: we will flag any subprocessor that requires access for operational reasons (e.g., telemetry for reliability) and describe mitigation controls (encryption at rest/in transit, access controls, retention limits).
- SCCs: Redwood will execute updated SCCs for EU -> US transfers; if you require any bespoke transfer mechanism please flag.

I'll attach the attestation template (redwood-dnm-attestation-template.pdf) and the subprocessor CSV export. Once you confirm the clause language, we will finalize the attestation and evidence pack.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-dnm-attestation-template.pdf

From: TheraBio Legal <legal@therabio.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Li <emma@therabio.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 11:33:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Proposed DNM clause + SCC confirmation

Monica / Ben — thanks, that language looks promising. Two follow-ups from legal: 

1) Prompt/response ownership: can Redwood explicitly confirm that Customer retains exclusive ownership of prompts and generated outputs (no assignment of derivatives to Provider)? We need that in the DPA.
2) Evidence delivery format: prefer SFTP drop (customer-owned SFTP) for the audit exports. Can you confirm the file formats and an encryption mechanism?

Also attached a short Q&A doc with a few remaining clarifying points.

—TheraBio Legal
Attachment: TheraBio_legal_qs.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: TheraBio Legal <legal@therabio.com>, Emma Li <emma@therabio.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed DNM clause + SCC confirmation — commitments and delivery plan

Thanks — quick consolidated commitments and proposed delivery plan so procurement has a single checklist: 

Commitments (to be contractually bound):
- DNM: Redwood will not use Customer prompts or generated outputs for model improvement; clause provided by Monica will be included in the DPA.
- Ownership: Customer retains all rights to prompts and generated outputs; Redwood will not claim derivative IP.
- Subprocessor disclosure: We will provide the CSV with current subprocessors and indicate which entities can access decrypted content (attached: redwood-subprocessor-inventory.csv).
- Evidence pack: Includes one-page signed attestation, audit log exports (CSV of access/export events), and a subprocessor access log. Delivery format: SFTP drop (customer SFTP) with AES-256-encrypted archives and pre-shared key + rotation instructions.
- Transfers: We will sign SCCs for EU -> US transfers if those transfers are required; where possible we will pin inference to EU-region endpoints.

Proposed timeline:
- Today (Thu): deliver subprocessor CSV (attached) and confirm SFTP details (please send host/creds or provide a contact).
- Fri: Laura delivers preliminary audit log extract and redwood delivers signed one-page attestation.
- Next Tue: full evidence pack (archived, checksummed) delivered to your SFTP.

Please confirm SFTP endpoint or if you prefer a secure Drive link instead. If procurement wants the attestation earlier we can provide a signed scan today. Once you confirm the SFTP details and ownership language, we'll mark this as ready for signature.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this piece.
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood-subprocessor-inventory.csv
